# TLS Foundations

> New Mexico foundation repair company. We don't guess a fix and work backward; we read the site and let the remedy follow. 55 combined years of New Mexico foundation and geotechnical experience.

TLS Foundations serves all 33 counties across five geologically distinct regions of New Mexico. The core position: New Mexico has more soil variation than most states -- 33 counties, 16 geologic basins -- so a repair approach calibrated for one region can be the wrong call two miles away, in another part of the same region. Investigation and repair are kept as separate revenue streams on purpose: TLS Foundations and its affiliate SandiaGEO (https://www.sandiageo.com) are owned by the same principals, so a recommendation follows the evidence, not the invoice. Outside New Mexico, the same principals also operate Foundation Repair Advocate (https://www.foundationrepairadvocate.com), an independent floor-survey and second-opinion service for homeowners in Arizona's White Mountains.

## Core

- [Home](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/): 55 years of New Mexico foundation and geotechnical experience -- investigation before diagnosis, always.
- [Why NM's Different](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/our-approach): New Mexico has more soil variation than most states. 33 counties, 16 geologic basins -- a repair approach built around that, not a national playbook.
- [Why Foundations Move](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/why-foundations-move): Foundations move because soil moves, and in New Mexico no two soils move the same way. The reference on causes, symptoms, and underpinning.
- [Common Concerns](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/common-concerns): Eighteen questions New Mexico homeowners actually search for. Answered honestly -- cost, signs, settlement vs. heave, insurance, warranties, and more.
- [Services](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/foundation-repair-methods): We match the repair method to the problem, not the other way around. Helical piers, push piers, grouting, drainage -- all based on a proper diagnosis.
- [Contact Us](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/contact-us): Text or call and you reach the owner(s). TLS Foundations and SandiaGEO keep investigation and repair separate -- recommendations follow evidence, not invoice.

## City Pages

- [Albuquerque, NM](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/albuquerque-nm): Where you live in Albuquerque determines what's wrong with your foundation -- West Mesa, North Valley, South Valley, East Side, and the Heights.
- [Rio Rancho, NM](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/rio-rancho-nm): Foundation repair in Rio Rancho, NM. Variable West Mesa sandy loam, inconsistent caliche, and pocket clays across six decades of construction.
- [Santa Fe, NM](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/santa-fe-nm): Santa Fe foundation repair requires local knowledge -- expansive clay, collapsible soils, and 400 years of adobe construction few contractors understand.

## NM Soils

- [Soil Roadmap](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/new-mexico-soil-conditions): All 33 New Mexico counties. Five regions organized by soil behavior -- the roadmap to how foundation repair should be approached in each.
- [Northern New Mexico](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/northern-new-mexico): Taos Plateau, Mora Valley, and Raton Basin -- frost heave at elevation, montmorillonite clays, and coal mine subsidence unique to Raton.
- [Central New Mexico](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/central-new-mexico): Albuquerque, Española, and Estancia basins -- collapsible West Mesa soils, river clays, Tesuque Formation shifts, and evaporite dissolution.
- [Four Corners](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/four-corners): San Juan Basin & Mancos Shale -- New Mexico's most misdiagnosed foundation environment. Heave that looks like settlement, plus collapsible river deposits.
- [Eastern New Mexico](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/eastern-new-mexico): High Plains, Pecos Valley, Mimbres and Lordsburg basins -- expansive clays, Permian evaporite dissolution, aquifer subsidence, and collapsible alluvium.
- [Southern New Mexico](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/southern-new-mexico): Mesilla, Hatch-Rincon, Tularosa, Sacramento Mountains, and Jornada del Muerto -- collapsible La Mesa soils, gypsum dissolution, and first-wetting collapse.

## Reference

- [Glossary](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/glossary): Plain-language definitions of foundation repair and soil science terms -- from acequia to underpinning. Browse and link directly to any term.
- [Expansive Soil](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/expansive-soil): Why foundations move with the seasons in New Mexico -- the science of expansive clay soils, how they damage foundations, and what a real evaluation looks at.
- [Collapsible Soil](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/collapsible-soil): Collapsible soils are New Mexico's most deceptive foundation hazard -- stable for decades, then gone in a season. Understanding the mechanism is the first step.
- [Job Notes](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/job-notes): Short, dated field notes from real diagnostic calls -- genericized, no names or addresses, written up as they happen. New entries publish on their own schedule, not a fixed one.

## Job Notes (currently live)

New entries publish on their own irregular schedule -- this list reflects what's live as of the last update to this file, not a complete archive. See the Job Notes index above for the current full set.

- [Swamp-Cooler Season](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/job-notes/swamp-cooler-season): Why doors that stick in July and loosen by October are usually moisture, not a failing foundation.
- [The Bid That Treated Heave as Settlement](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/job-notes/bid-that-treated-heave-as-settlement): A crack that opened every summer and closed every winter got a settlement bid anyway. The calendar was already telling the real story.
- [Fill Under the Slab, Native Soil Under the Addition](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/job-notes/fill-under-the-slab): One house, two foundations, two completely different soil profiles a few feet apart -- and why treating them the same was the mistake.
- [The Condensate Line](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/job-notes/the-condensate-line): The AC condensate line most people never think about -- and why a summer of drips in one spot is enough to move expansive clay.
- [Caliche Stopped the Helix](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/job-notes/caliche-stopped-the-helix): A helical pier's torque spikes against a caliche layer -- and why a high number on the gauge isn't the same thing as bearing capacity.
- [We Told Them Not to Pier It](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/job-notes/we-told-them-not-to-pier-it): Three pier bids were ready to schedule on a house whose crack had paint in it and a door that had already eased back by October -- the honest answer was not this week.

## Interactive Tools

- [Symptom Guide](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/symptom-guide): See something? Here's what it usually means and whether it warrants attention -- New Mexico foundation symptoms grouped by category and soil context.
- [Cause Library](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/cause-library): Every mechanism that moves a New Mexico foundation, ranked by whether underpinning is actually the right call or something else needs to happen first.
- [Printable Crack Gauge](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/crack-gauge): A free printable gauge for measuring crack width at home, plus what the measurement actually means.
- [Send Us Photos](https://www.tlsfoundations.com/send-photos): Send photos of what you're seeing for an initial read before anyone visits in person.
